description: Assumes one ProjectManager can manage multiple Projects despite explicitly acknowledging that the prompt does not specify this multiplicity.
Resolves the ambiguous Team–Project relationship using what is "typical" or "simple" rather than preserving the ambiguity in the requirements.

Assumes that multiple External scenes can share the same Location, producing the multiplicity External "*" --> "1" Location. The reasoning explicitly bases this on “typically yes,” while the prompt only states that each external scene is filmed at a location.

Uses composition between Scene and Setup by assuming that deleting a scene would delete its setups. The prompt establishes that each setup belongs to one scene, but it does not specify lifecycle dependency.
Uses composition between Setup and Take without establishing that a take’s lifecycle is controlled by its setup. The prompt specifies association and multiplicity, not composite ownership.

Introduces a WordProcessor controller/application class with operations such as createNewDocument(), openDocument(), saveDocument(), and printDocument(), although the prompt describes user actions but does not specify such a domain class.

Omits the explicitly mentioned Column class because representing a table only through rows and cells is considered “typical” and simpler, rather than modelling both rows and columns as stated in the prompt.
Introduces the interfaces IBodyContent and ICellContent primarily to solve a design/reuse problem created during modelling; neither abstraction is suggested by the prompt.

Models text inside a table cell as a simplified TextContent string instead of using the already-derived sentence–word–character structure, explicitly choosing simplicity over a consistent representation of the stated text structure.

Introduces Receptionist and Nurse as persistent domain classes (and later a Staff hierarchy), although the prompt only describes them as system users. Only Doctor is explicitly stated to have maintained information.

Introduces a separate Prescription class (linking Visit and Medication) even though the prompt only states that multiple medications may be prescribed during a visit. The intermediate abstraction is an unsupported design decision.

Chooses to model the actors (Receptionist, Nurse, Doctor) as system classes with operations because it seems like a "complete model," shifting from modelling the described domain entities toward modelling system users and responsibilities.

Interprets “when a movie is not available it is ordered” as a shop-restocking process and introduces RestockOrder and Supplier. The text does not mention suppliers or establish that the order is a stock-replenishment order rather than a customer order for an unavailable movie.

Assumes that each PurchaseOrder and RentalOrder concerns exactly one Movie, explicitly choosing this representation “for simplicity” even though the number of movies associated with an order is not specified.

Uses composition between Subscriber and Card based only on the statement that subscribers use their “own card.” Ownership or exclusive use does not establish that the card’s lifecycle depends on the subscriber.

Equates the flight’s unspecified pilot role with captain and replaces the stated pilot association with a captain association. The description mentions a pilot and co-pilot for each flight, while captain appears separately as an example of a role required by an aircraft type.

Repeatedly misinterprets UML association-end multiplicities and finally uses Flight "1" -- "*" Pilot for both captain and co-pilot. This notation allows multiple pilots at each role for one flight rather than expressing that each flight has exactly one pilot and one co-pilot.
Uses composition between Bank and Customer. The statement that the bank system stores customer data does not establish that customers are lifecycle-dependent parts of a Bank object.
Uses composition between Customer and Account without evidence that an account’s lifecycle is exclusively controlled by one customer. The prompt also does not rule out jointly held accounts.

Uses composition between InvestmentAccount and StockOrder. The prompt establishes that investment accounts are used to buy stocks, but it does not establish lifecycle ownership of stock orders by the account.

Assumes that the same PartAccessory can be fitted in multiple assembly services by reinterpreting it as a reusable product type. The presence of a serial number instead suggests that each instance may represent an individual physical item.

Models AssemblyService–PartAccessory with 0..* at both ends. This permits a part/accessory to exist without being associated with any assembly service, despite the explicit rule that parts and accessories are sold only together with an assembly service.

Reverses the association-end multiplicities for Dish–Ingredient. The final notation Dish "1..*" -- "0..*" Ingredient allows a dish to contain zero ingredients, although the reasoning correctly states that every dish must contain multiple ingredients.
Uses Meal "*" -- "*" Dish, allowing a meal to contain no dishes. This fails to represent the explicit requirement that several dishes are consumed in every meal.

Reverses the multiplicities for the Customer–DeliveryCenter association. The final notation Customer "1" -- "0..*" DeliveryCenter allows each customer to be associated with multiple delivery centers and each delivery center with exactly one customer, contrary to the requirement that every customer has one associated delivery center while a center may serve many customers.

Assumes that each Furniture piece belongs to exactly one FurnitureLine. The prompt states that each line consists of several pieces, but does not rule out the same furniture piece appearing in multiple lines. The reasoning explicitly chooses one-to-many “for simplicity.”

Reverses the association-end multiplicities for Furniture–Component. The final notation Furniture "1..*" -- "0..*" Component permits a furniture piece to have no components and requires every component to be used in at least one furniture piece. The prompt instead says every furniture piece consists of several components.

Introduces a separate Material entity and relationship even though the specification only states that all products of the same type are made from the same material. No attributes or identity for Material are given, so creating it is an unsupported design assumption.

Introduces a separate Skill entity and many-to-many relationship, although the specification only requires storing "a list of skills" for each worker. Representing skills as an entity rather than a multivalued attribute is an unsupported modeling assumption.

Collapses Reservation and Rental into a single Rental class with optional actualBike and returnDate. The prompt explicitly distinguishes reservations from rentals, so treating them as one entity is an unsupported structural decision.

Reverses the multiplicities for the Rental–Bike association. The proposed notation Rental "0..1" -- "*" Bike allows one rental to reference many bikes and restricts each bike to at most one rental, whereas a rental may have at most one actual bike and the same bike may appear in multiple rentals over time.

Introduces an ExitSensor class and makes it part of the parking system. The prompt states only that the exit barrier rises automatically when a car wishes to leave; it does not identify a sensor or specify the mechanism responsible for detecting the car.

Reverses the multiplicities for Client–Account. The final notation Client "0..*" -- "1..*" Account allows an account to have no owners and requires each client to own at least one account. To support optional customer ownership and joint accounts, each account should have 1..* clients, while a client may own 0..* accounts.

Reverses the multiplicities for the personal-banker association. The notation Client "1" -- "0..*" Employee allows one client to have multiple personal bankers and limits an employee to one client, contrary to the requirement that each customer has one personal banker while an employee may serve multiple customers.

Adds the constraint that a Book can have at most one active Borrow at a time. The prompt limits how many books a user may borrow, but it does not state that each Book represents a single physical copy or prohibit simultaneous loans of the same title.

Uses User "1" -- "0..*" Book for the borrowing association. This restricts each book to one user across the association while allowing each user many books, which cannot represent the stated borrowing history in which a book may be borrowed by different users at different times.

Models WebUser as a subclass of Customer. The text describes web-user registration as an optional role or account capability that a customer may acquire, rather than establishing an “is-a” specialization.

Assumes that every Payment is associated with exactly one Order through Order "1" -- "0..*" Payment. The prompt only says that an order may refer to several payments and that each payment belongs to exactly one Account; it does not state that a payment can be referenced by only one order.

Uses composition from both Order and ShoppingCart to the same LineItem class. Without an explicit {xor} constraint or separate line-item subclasses, the model permits a LineItem to have two composite owners, which violates UML composition semantics.
